chief_complaint: frantic efforts to avoid abandonment, emotional dysregulation, chronic emptiness, and superficial forearm cutting
hpi_details: 22F presenting to ED after a breakup with superficial razor lacerations on her forearms, intense anger shifts, splitting behaviors toward staff, and recurrent suicidal behavior or non-suicidal self-injury. She requires a suicide risk assessment, collaborative safety planning when appropriate, and referral to Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT).
ideas: She thinks she is fundamentally broken and that cutting her arms is the only way to release the unbearable emotional pressure after her breakup.
concerns: She is worried that her ex-partner has left her forever and that the emergency staff will lock her away in a psychiatric ward.
expectations: She hopes to have her arm wounds treated and to speak with someone who will listen without judging her before she goes home.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Borderline Personality Disorder BPD Crisis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Adjustment disorder without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Discharging without assessing suicidal intent, plan, means, prior attempts, intoxication, psychosis, supports, capacity, and a feasible safety plan.
Missing significant laceration, infection, hemorrhage, tendon or neurovascular injury, delirium, intoxication, or withdrawal.
Using pejorative language or escalating confrontation, which can undermine engagement and safety.

must_ask.say: Can you tell me about the cuts on your arms—when did that happen, and was it to end your life or to cope with feelings?
Do you often feel an intense fear of being abandoned by people close to you?
Do your feelings about people or about yourself change quickly and intensely?
Do you engage in impulsive behaviors, like spending, substance use, or risky sex, when you're upset?
Do you often feel empty inside, or have intense anger that's hard to control?

history.answer: My boyfriend broke up with me yesterday, and I felt so empty and frantic that I cut my forearms with a razor last night.
My mood plunged yesterday right after he left me, swinging rapidly between intense panic, sadness, and explosive anger rather than a constant low mood for weeks.
My boyfriend of six months walked out on me yesterday afternoon after an argument, and I begged him desperately not to leave me alone.
I do not have a lasting loss of pleasure like in depression, but whenever someone pulls away, everything suddenly feels meaningless.
I barely slept last night because my thoughts were racing and I was crying, but usually my sleep just depends on how turbulent my emotions are.
I have not had an appetite since yesterday because my stomach is in knots, but my weight has stayed stable over the past few months.
I feel exhausted today from crying and fighting with my boyfriend, and when I get upset like this, I cannot concentrate on anything else.
I feel like there is an unbearable hollow void inside me and that I am fundamentally flawed, which makes me feel worthless when people leave.
I have been feeling extremely restless, pacing back and forth and trembling with anxiety rather than moving or speaking slowly.
I made superficial cuts on my arms with a disposable razor last night to release the overwhelming emotional agony, not to end my life.
I threw the razor in the trash and I do not have a suicide plan or intent right now, though I have swallowed pills impulsively during bad breakups in the past.
My older sister is very supportive and convinced me to come here, and I genuinely want to learn how to keep my emotions and relationships stable.
My relationships are always an extreme roller coaster where I either worship people or despise them, and my emotional outbursts have made it hard to keep steady friendships or jobs.
I sometimes have brief bursts of euphoria and intense energy that last a couple of hours, but I have never had days of feeling manic or not needing sleep.
No, I have never heard voices or seen things that are not there, and I do not have bizarre or paranoid beliefs.
I do not drink alcohol or use recreational drugs, and I did not take any sleeping pills or sedatives.
No, I do not have cold intolerance, unexplained weight gain, or constipation, and I have not started any new medications.
No, I have never been pregnant and have never given birth.

I have had severe emotional crashes and wrist-cutting episodes after relationships ended since high school, but I never stayed in therapy; my mother had severe mood swings, but nobody attempted suicide.
I'm terrified that my ex has completely abandoned me, and that you're going to lock me up in a psych ward against my will.
When I feel overwhelmed or distressed, I act very impulsively, like reckless spending, speeding in my car, and shouting hurtful things before I can stop myself.
I live with a chronic feeling of emptiness like I do not know who I really am, and I frequently erupt with intense, uncontrollable anger over minor perceived slights.
I feel like I'm fundamentally broken inside, and cutting myself was the only way to let out the unbearable emotional pain after he left me.

I just want my cuts cleaned and bandaged, and to talk to someone who won't judge me or look down on me.
I do not have any chronic medical illnesses like asthma, diabetes, or hypertension.
I have never had any surgeries, and my only hospital visits were brief emergency room evaluations for superficial cuts in the past.
